building.name: International Building Code, adopted with amendments as the Building Code of the City of Saint Louis by Ordinance 70794 (Board Bill 53CS, session 2018-2019), amended by Ordinance 71742 (securing vacant buildings)
building.local_amendments_note: Ordinance 70794 replaces Chapter 1 (administration, including Section 105 on permits) with the city's own, amends parts of Chapters 2 to 7, 9, 11, 12, 14 to 16, 18, 31 to 33 and 35, deletes Chapter 27 (see the Electrical Code) and deletes Chapter 29, Plumbing Systems, in its entirety (see the Plumbing Code). It makes no change to Chapter 8 (interior finishes, so Section 803.9 on HDPE stands) or to Chapter 10 (Table 1004.5, floor area per occupant). In Chapter 12 it changes only Section 1205.3.3, so Section 1209.3 (toilet compartments and urinal partitions) stands. Chapter 11 amendments add a waiver procedure through the Commissioner on the Disabled (1103.3, 1103.4) and site routes (1104.7); none concerns toilet rooms.
building.effective_note: The Building Division's list of adopted codes gives 'Date adopted: 08-01-18'. The ordinance has an emergency clause ('effective immediately upon its approval by the Mayor'), and the ordinance's own page shows 'Effective: 07/06/2018', which is the date of its third reading. The Mayor's approval date was not read.
building.quote: SECTION TWO. ADOPTION. The 2018 International Building Code as published by the International Code Council, Inc., one copy of which is on file in the Office of the Register of the City of Saint Louis, being marked and designated as the International Building Code, including Appendices E, F, G, H, I, and J, is hereby adopted as the Building Code of the City of Saint Louis, in the State of Missouri [...] CHAPTERS 27 AND 29 ARE AMENDED AS FOLLOWS: Delete Chapter 27 in its entirety. Refer to the Electrical Code. Delete Chapter 29 in its entirety. Refer to the Plumbing Code.

plumbing.name: Uniform Plumbing Code, adopted with amendments as the Plumbing Code of the City of Saint Louis by Ordinance 71644 (Board Bill 182, session 2022-2023)
plumbing.local_amendments_note: Ordinance 71644 replaces Chapter 1 and amends the other chapters. In Chapter 4 it adds Section 423.0 (food service establishments), restates the heading text of the Minimum Plumbing Facilities table and gives the table its own Notes 1 to 20. It does not reprint the table's rows and does not amend Sections 422.1 (count, half and half, rounding), 422.2 (separate facilities and exceptions) or 422.2.1 (single-use signs). It repeals Ordinance 69255 (2009 Uniform Plumbing Code, 2012), which had its own city-written fixture table (Table 4-1), only 'insofar as it conflicts'. The published PDF of Ordinance 71644 has the repealed Ordinance 69255 attached after page 222.

amendment.text: St. Louis deletes the building code's plumbing chapter, so the toilet count comes from the city's Plumbing Code: Table 422.1 of the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code with the city's own notes. Urinals are a required column of that table. City note 14: women's toilets at least equal men's toilets plus urinals (not in retail or wholesale stores). City note 5: each urinal beyond the minimum may replace one men's toilet, down to two thirds of the required toilets. City Section 423.0: a food service establishment with an occupant load of 100 or more needs separate employee and customer facilities, and employee facilities are not counted in the restaurant numbers (note 11(B)); customer load is one person per 15 square feet of dining and waiting area, outdoor seating included. City note 15: public areas of small offices (banks, dental, law, real estate offices and similar) use the store row. Unamended 2021 text: half male and half female, fractions rounded up (422.1); one single-user room for both sexes where the total occupant load is 10 or fewer, or 50 or fewer in business and mercantile occupancies (422.2).
amendment.quote: Each building shall be provided with sanitary facilities, including provisions for persons with disabilities as prescribed by the Department having jurisdiction. Table 422.1 applies to new buildings, additions to a building, and changes of occupancy or type in an existing building resulting in increased occupant load. [...] 5. For each urinal added in excess of the minimum required, one (1) water closet may be deducted. The number of water closets shall not be reduced to less than two-thirds (2/3) of the minimum requirement. [...] 11. A restaurant is defined as a business which sells food to be consumed on the premises. [...] (B) Employee toilet facilities are not to be included in the above restaurant requirements. [...] 14. The total number of water closets for females shall be at least equal to the total number of water closets and urinals provided for men. This requirement does not apply to retail or wholesale stores. [...] 423.0 Food Service Establishments. Food service establishments with an occupant load of one hundred (100) or more shall be provided with separate facilities for employees and customers. Customer and employee facilities may be combined for occupant loads less than one hundred (100). Customer occupant load shall be determined as one occupant per each 15 square foot or part thereof, of dining and waiting area.

table_rows.restaurant: A-2 Assembly occupancy (restaurants, pubs, lounges, nightclubs and banquet halls): water closets Male 1: 1-50, 2: 51-150, 3: 151-300, 4: 301-400; Female 1: 1-25, 2: 26-50, 3: 51-100, 4: 101-200, 6: 201-300, 8: 301-400; urinals Male 1: 1-200, 2: 201-300, 3: 301-400, 4: 401-600
table_rows.school: E Educational occupancy (private or public schools): water closets Male 1 per 50, Female 1 per 30; urinals Male 1 per 100
table_rows.read_note: Read in the text layer of IAPMO's free read-only edition of the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code (pages 34 to 39). The table's cells come out of that layer out of order; the bands match the same rows of the 2018 and 2024 editions as other packs in this project read them.

model_quotes.split_and_rounding: 422.1 [...] The minimum number of fixtures shall be calculated at 50 percent male and 50 percent female based on the total occupant load. Where information submitted indicates a difference in the distribution of the sexes such information shall be used to determine the number of fixtures for each sex. [...] Where applying the fixture ratios in Table 422.1 results in fractional numbers, such numbers shall be rounded to the next whole number.
model_quotes.separate_facilities: 422.2 Separate Facilities. Separate toilet facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: (1) Residential installations. (2) In occupancies with a total occupant load of 10 or less, including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (3) In business and mercantile occupancies with a total occupant load of 50 or less including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes.

worked_examples.how: 25 of each sex. Business row: men 1 toilet (1-50) and 1 urinal (1-100); women 2 toilets (16-30).
50 of each sex. Men 1 toilet (1-50) and 1 urinal (1-100); women 3 toilets (31-50).
100 of each sex. Men 2 toilets (51-100) and 1 urinal (1-100); women 4 toilets (51-100).
200 of each sex. Men 3 toilets (101-200) and 2 urinals (101-200); women 8 toilets (101-200).

25 of each sex. A-2 row: men 1 toilet (1-50) and 1 urinal (1-200); women 1 toilet (1-25), raised to 2 because the women's toilets may not be fewer than the men's toilets and urinals together (city note 14, model note 3).
50 of each sex. Men 1 toilet (1-50) and 1 urinal (1-200); women 2 toilets (26-50). At an occupant load of 100 or more, Section 423.0 also requires separate employee facilities, not counted here.
100 of each sex. Men 2 toilets (51-150) and 1 urinal (1-200); women 3 toilets (51-100). Separate employee facilities are extra (423.0).
200 of each sex. Men 3 toilets (151-300) and 1 urinal (1-200); women 4 toilets (101-200). Separate employee facilities are extra (423.0).
25 of each sex. E row: men 1 per 50 = 1 toilet, urinals 1 per 100 = 1; women 1 per 30 = 1, raised to 2 by the women's-toilets rule.
50 of each sex. Men 1 toilet, 1 urinal; women 50/30 = 1.67, rounded up to 2.
100 of each sex. Men 2 toilets, 1 urinal; women 100/30 = 3.33, rounded up to 4.
200 of each sex. Men 4 toilets, 2 urinals; women 200/30 = 6.67, rounded up to 7.

fixtures.open_point: Ordinance 71644 gives notes numbered 1 to 20, which follow the footnotes of the city's former Table 4-1 (Ordinance 69255), but refers to 'Table 422.1' and does not reprint any rows; Ordinance 69255 is repealed only where it conflicts. The worked examples use the rows of the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code's Table 422.1. Whether the Building Division's plumbing plan review still applies any row of the former city table (for offices it had fewer men's toilets and no urinal below 101 men) was not found on an official page.
fixtures.hdpe_fire: Applies. St. Louis adopted the 2018 International Building Code with no amendment to Chapter 8, so Section 803.9 (HDPE and polypropylene interior finish must meet the NFPA 286 room test, quoted in the Missouri state pack) is in force.
fixtures.occupant_load: Unamended Table 1004.5 of the 2018 International Building Code (business areas 150 gross, assembly with tables and chairs 15 net, classroom 20 net, quoted in the state pack). The Plumbing Code's Section 423.0 sets the customer load of a food service establishment at one per 15 square feet of dining and waiting area, outdoor seating included.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 105.2 Work exempt from permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of the City of Saint Louis. Permits shall not be required for the following: 1. Tuckpointing, ordinary or minor repair to exterior masonry, exterior painting, or similar repair or finish work; [...] 12. Interior painting, floor sanding and refinishing, floor tile or carpeting, replacement of flooring with like material, application of wallpaper and other wall covering material, moveable cases, counters and partitions, and cabinet installation, counter tops, and similar finish work; 13. Plaster patching or gypsum board replacement not exceeding 25% of the total wall or ceiling area of a room or space provided the fire rating and moisture resistance is maintained and no modifications are made; 14. Wall paneling of any type when applied directly to existing room wall surfaces; [...] 16. Nonfixed or moveable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet nine inches in height; 17. Foundation and floor slab repair [...]
permit.note: Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. Items 12 and 16 exempt 'moveable' and 'nonfixed' partitions (item 16 up to 5 feet 9 inches); whether the Building Division reads a floor-anchored or overhead-braced toilet partition as moveable is not stated. Items 18 to 30 apply only to dwellings of up to four units. Exceptions to the list: disaster repairs, flood plain sites and work under the Cultural Resources Office.
permit.general_rule_quote: 105.1 Required. Any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to perform site grading or excavation; to construct, enlarge, alter, make non-ordinary repairs to, move, or demolish a building or structure; to change the occupancy of a building, structure, or premises from one use group to another or to change to a prohibited use; or to cause any such work to be done [...] shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permits.
permit.repairs_quote: 105.2.2 Repairs. Application or notice to the building official is not required for ordinary repairs to structures, replacement of lamps, or the connection of approved portable electrical equipment to approved permanently installed receptacles. Such repairs shall not include the cutting away of any wall, partition, or portion thereof; the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support; or the removal or change of any required means of egress or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements.
permit.city_page_quote: A building permit is required when any structural change or major alteration is made to an existing building or when any new construction is undertaken. Normal building maintenance does not require a building permit in most instances, but it's best to check and see if your type of work is listed as requiring a permit. [...] Interior/Exterior Alterations: Most interior/exterior alteration projects require permitting, particularly if they impacting load-bearing walls or structure elements.

restrooms_city.note: No city ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found. Ordinance 71644 leaves the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code's Sections 422.2, 422.2.1 and 422.2.2 unamended: single-use and family or assisted-use toilet facilities carry a sign indicating use by either sex; separate facilities for each sex are required above the small-occupancy limits; the 2021 text has no exception for a shared multi-stall room for all genders; two family or assisted-use rooms may replace separate rooms where each sex needs only one toilet. City additions touching the subject: Section 423.0 (the second employee toilet room in a large food service establishment 'shall be uni-sex'). A web search returned news reports of a mayoral executive order on all-gender restrooms in city government buildings; it was not read on an official page and is not a rule for private buildings.
restrooms_city.quote: 422.2.1 Single Use Toilet Facilities. Single use toilet facilities and family or assisted use toilet facilities shall be identified with signage indicating use by either sex. 422.2.2 Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Facilities. Where a separate toilet facility is required for each sex, and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted in place of the required separate toilet facilities.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to St. Louis job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the city's stall counts, rules and tax.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for St. Louis offices, schools, hospitals and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** St. Louis's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** St. Louis sets the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Missouri has no state law on single-user or all-gender restrooms, and none on who may use which restroom. Under St. Louis's plumbing rules a one-person or family restroom carries a sign showing that either sex may use it. Larger buildings need separate men's and women's rooms, and the rules have no provision for a shared all-gender room with stalls. Where each sex needs only one toilet, two family restrooms may take the place of the separate rooms.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** St. Louis's list of work that needs no building permit includes movable cases, counters and partitions, cabinet installation and similar finish work, and non-fixed partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the Building Division's Permit Section at (314) 622-3313 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of St. Louis Building Division
page.stalls_intro: Missouri has no statewide building code, so the City of St. Louis's own rules decide. The city counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and women get more toilets than men. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are required in men's rooms, each with a screen, and the women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together. The table shows women's stalls / men's stalls + urinals.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A restaurant designed for 100 people or more also needs separate staff restrooms, which the table doesn't count. An office or shop designed for 50 people or fewer, or any building designed for 10 or fewer, may have one single-user restroom for everyone instead of separate rooms. A men's room may swap a toilet for each urinal added beyond the required number, as long as two thirds of its required toilets remain. Confirm the count for your building with the City of St. Louis Building Division.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, St. Louis's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor and a classroom at one per 20. The city's plumbing rules count a restaurant at one person per 15 square feet of dining and waiting area, outdoor seating included. Your architect or the Building Division sets the final number.
skip_state_sources: Toilet counts under the model rules
No Missouri restroom-use law in force
page.install_rule: Building, building maintenance and carpentry contractors, among other listed trades, need a City of St. Louis license from the License Collector. Missouri has no state license for general or specialty interior contractors such as partition installers. Confirm what your project needs with the License Collector and the Building Division. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Missouri has no state license for partition installers, and building and carpentry contractors need a City of St. Louis license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, city, county and school district projects with a total cost above $75,000, Missouri law requires at least the wage the state sets each year for each trade in each county. The City of St. Louis has its own rate, separate from St. Louis County's. For a carpenter on building work in the city that is $69.16 an hour, benefits included.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.679% at most addresses in the City of St. Louis: 4.225% state and 5.454% city. The city is not part of St. Louis County, so no county tax applies. Many small business and transportation districts, several of them downtown, add 1% or 2%. Partitions shipped in from a seller outside Missouri fall under the use tax instead, 9.013% at most city addresses.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, clinics and university buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel that stands up to frequent disinfecting, with full-height privacy options.
